subject: HarborPay access handoff — SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service account naming
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@harborpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HarborPay access handoff — SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service account naming

Hi Alex — great to meet you last week. I'm Evelyn on the Customer Success team and I'll be coordinating the access controls handoff for HarborPay's production cutover. Quick priorities for the kickoff call so we can align engineering and security: 

- SSO (SAML) metadata and ACS/Entity IDs for production vs staging
- SCIM provisioning mapping and bulk provisioning template for ~1,200 users
- IP allowlist + expected egress IPs for inbound traffic to our tokens endpoint
- Service account naming convention + least-privilege roles for service-to-service calls
- Org policies (session length, device controls) and audit log requirements

I've attached our implementation checklist and a SCIM mapping template to help. Proposed next steps: 
1) Quick 30–45m kickoff with your security and identity engineer this week — when are you available?
2) Share SAML metadata (IdP cert and metadata XML), and a test SCIM user in staging
3) Confirm which Redwood-managed IPs you need to allow (we will provide exact ranges)

Can you loop in your security/identity contact (or confirm the best address)? We aim for a staged cutover in the week of Nov 8 with a canary group.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0193

Attachments: redwood-sso-implementation-checklist.pdf (implementation checklist), scim-mapping-template.csv (SCIM attribute map)
From: Alex Porter <aporter@harborpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@harborpay.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HarborPay access handoff — SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service account naming

Evelyn — thanks, this is perfect. I'm HarborPay's identity lead. Looping in our security mailbox for the audit/logging details. Quick answers to your bullets: 

- SAML: we'll provide IdP metadata XML and cert. Staging entity ID is https://staging.harborpay.com/saml, prod is https://portal.harborpay.com/saml.
- SCIM: we prefer SCIM push provisioning. We'll send a small test user in staging (email: ci+scimtest@harborpay.com).
- IP allowlist: we need a list of Redwood egress ranges to allow outbound webhook callbacks. We also have an inbound whitelist (we control firewall) — can you provide token endpoint ranges?
- Service accounts: agree on least-privilege. Our naming convention is rp-{team}-{purpose}; we can accept redwood-sa-{customer}-env if you prefer.
- Audit: HarborPay requires 90-day retention for auth logs and an exportable CSV to our SIEM weekly.

We can do a kickoff Thurs 21 Oct at 2pm PT or Fri 22 Oct at 9am PT. Either works for our team.

Alex Porter
Identity Lead, Security | HarborPay
aporter@harborpay.com | +1 202-555-0114
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HarborPay access handoff — prep notes (IP ranges + SA naming)

Eve / Jonas — quick internal note ahead of the kickoff. I prefilled the attached checklist with the HarborPay-specific items and flagged a few open questions for engineering: 

- Token endpoint IPs: prod egress currently uses the shared Redwood NAT pool for hosted customers; per-customer dedicated egress is available on Dedicated but requires a config change. We should confirm whether HarborPay expects dedicated egress IPs or whether they can accept the shared range plus cert-based verification.
- SCIM rate limits: HarborPay's user count (~1,200) suggests we should propose a batching cadence (100 users / 10s) to avoid throttling.
- Service account naming: propose redwood-sa-harborpay-prod and redwood-sa-harborpay-staging; scope to 'provision_user' + 'read_audit'.
- Audit export: we can add a weekly CSV export via our console; need to confirm retention SLA — standard hosted is 30 days, Redwood Optimize addon supports 90/365 day retention.

Attachments: redwood-sso-implementation-checklist.pdf (filled), scim-mapping-template.csv (sample filled rows)

Action items before kickoff: Jonas to confirm NAT ranges or dedicated egress option; Eve to confirm proposed kickoff times with Alex; I'll pull the retention pricing band for 90 days.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HarborPay access handoff — technical answers and cutover plan

Folks — technical clarifications and a suggested cutover sequence. Notes below and I'll paste into the kickoff slide.

1) Egress IPs: For hosted customers we publish a set of stable NAT ranges. Prod egress ranges (current) — 34.210.128.0/20, 52.23.64.0/19, 18.196.0.0/16. If HarborPay has a strict inbound ACL, those are what they should allow for callback/webhook traffic. If they require single-address pinning, we can provision a dedicated egress on Redwood Dedicated (requires a one-week lead time and routing change).

2) SAML metadata: our ACS endpoint for prod will be https://api.redwood.ai/v1/saml/acs/harborpay and staging https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/saml/acs/harborpay. We will send SP metadata after you confirm entity IDs.

3) SCIM mapping: attached is a sample mapping. For HarborPay the canonical attributes are displayName, userName (email), externalId (employeeID), groups. We recommend an initial full sync of 1,200 users during a low-traffic window overnight with incremental syncs thereafter.

4) Service accounts & roles: I agree with the naming Monica suggested. Implementation detail: service accounts are scoped with OAuth tokens and tied to a customer namespace; I'll prepare a minimal IAM role 'scim:provision' and 'audit:read' for redwood-sa-harborpay-prod.

5) Audit retention: engineering can enable 90-day retention via the 'compliance-retention' tier. Monica — I'll coordinate with billing to update the plan once HarborPay confirms.

Proposed cutover timeline (high level):
- T+0 (pre-cutover): exchange SAML metadata; provision service accounts and IP allowlist test
- T+1 (staging): SCIM full sync to staging and verify group mappings (2–3 hours)
- T+3 (canary prod): enable SSO for 5% of users and monitor logs for 48 hours
- T+7 (full prod): open SSO to all users and start weekly audit exports

I'll join the kickoff and bring the exact NAT ranges and the scim-mapping-template.csv (attached).

Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Alex Porter <aporter@harborpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HarborPay access handoff — SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist & service account naming

Thanks all — Thurs 21 was tricky for us so Fri 22 at 9am PT worked best and that call was productive. Confirming the decisions from the kickoff: 

- HarborPay will allow the three Redwood NAT ranges you provided (security@harborpay.com has logged them).
- We'll take the redwood-sa-harborpay-prod / -staging naming. Please provision 'scim:provision' and 'audit:read' roles.
- We'll test SCIM in staging using the provided mapping CSV; target full staged sync Tue 26 Oct at 02:00 PT during our low window.
- Audit retention: we will purchase the 90-day retention add-on after contract amendment. Please send DocuSign for the add-on (reference deal D-48721).

Next steps: Evelyn, please send the SP metadata and the DocuSign link; Monica / Jonas, please schedule a 1-hour follow-up for the staging runbook (tentatively Mon 25 Oct 11am PT).

Appreciate the clear plan — looking forward to the cutover.

Alex Porter
Identity Lead, Security | HarborPay
aporter@harborpay.com
